fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Verse 3 says, "I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors…" So the warriors are the ones summoned.

I can see why a judge would feel right at home in this scene. But no judges show up in verse 3. The text says, "I have commanded My sanctified ones; I have even summoned My warriors…" So the warriors are the ones summoned.
Melt is right. Verse 7 says, "…all hands will fall limp, and every man’s heart will melt." It's a picture of fear taking the strength right out of people.
That's the pair. Verse 11 says, "I will end the haughtiness of the arrogant and lay low the pride of the ruthless." The arrogant and the ruthless are the ones brought low, friend.
The verse says the opposite, friend. Verse 17 says the Medes "…have no regard for silver and no desire for gold." So the statement is false.

Yes. Verse 21 says, "But desert creatures will lie down there, and howling creatures will fill her houses. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will leap about." The old houses get a whole different crowd of residents.
